messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Paging eng-oncall: sudden spike in GPU driver Xid errors on cluster-gpu-prod-7 starting at 23:04 UTC. Source: node gpu-node-7b. Autoscaling events observed.

oncall-bot: @marisa you're on-call. Please acknowledge.

marisa: ack. looking now. pulling alerts and recent deploys. any customer reports?

ellie-cs: got a ticket from important-corp saying latency spiked and some requests failed with 502s ~23:05 UTC. They were hitting chat endpoints.

samir: checking node health: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-7b` shows multiple pods in CrashLoopBackOff. GPU driver module appears flapping.

leah: logs from kubelet show repeated container restarts and OOMKilled for the runner containers on that node.

ryan: pulling dmesg/syslog from node (snip):

```
[23:04:12] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[23:04:13] kernel: nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU fault detected: Xid 79, intr_flags 0x00000000
[23:04:14] ECC: Correctable error on GPU 0
```

samir: Xid 79 plus ECC events -> consistent with driver resets that cause NVML to drop and containers to die if pinned. Could be hardware noisy or driver regression.

marisa: any recent driver rollouts? infra-bot, did we push a node image?

infra-bot: No node image rollouts in last 48h. One GPU runtime config change 2 days ago (quantization patch) but no driver bump.

leah: to buy time let's cordon + drain the node and shift traffic. Command: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-7b && kubectl drain gpu-node-7b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

marisa: doing drain now. starting pod eviction. will watch for failover.

ellie-cs: telling important-corp we are investigating and shifting traffic; will provide ETA once stable.

samir: while draining, collecting `nvidia-smi -q` and persistent logs. `nvidia-smi -q` shows intermittent no-response periods.

ryan: recommend restarting nvidia-driver on node before putting back. Sequence: stop services -> rmmod nvidia_uvm nvidia -> modprobe nvidia. But careful with running containers.

marisa: ok node drained. running `sudo systemctl stop kubelet` then unloading driver.

leah: capturing kernel oops: `dmesg --since "23:03" | grep -i nvrm` -> multiple Xid 79/31 entries across 23:03-23:06.

samir: cross-check telemetry: dozens of short-lived spikes across multiple pods pinned to same GPU across the hour. Not seeing similar patterns on node-7a. Might be a single-GPU hardware fault.

marisa: after driver unload/load, gpu-node-7b is showing stable `nvidia-smi`. re-enabled kubelet and uncordoned. will slowly drain back workloads by re-scheduling critical pods first.

ryan: suggestion: apply node-level taint `gpu-faulty=true:NoSchedule` to prevent auto-placement until we confirm stability.

leah: applied taint. scheduling override for canary pods only.

marisa: rolling restarts of affected pods on other nodes to clear corrupted NVML state.

ellie-cs: update to important-corp: we shifted traffic and restarted GPU node, temporary mitigations in place; investigating root cause with hardware vendor if it resurfaces.

samir: saving logs and core dumps to /mnt/scratch/incident-2635000000/ (nv-hostengine logs, nvidia-bug-report.log). Will escalate to hardware team with vendor ticket including attached `dmesg` and `nvidia-bug-report.log`.

infra-bot: Created vendor ticket VND-9241: includes logs, timeseries of ECC correctable counts and Xid events.

marisa: monitoring now for 20m. alert thresholds lowered for ECC/Xid so we'll catch recurrences quickly.

ryan: recommended post-incident action items: 1) mark GPU slot for hardware inspection/re-RMA if repeats. 2) add automated node taint on Xid surge. 3) add runbook steps for safe driver reload during live traffic.

leah: adding runbook note: prefer controlled drain then `systemctl stop kubelet` before rmmod to avoid container deadlocks.

samir: customer impact summary for postmortem: Important-Corp experienced elevated 95th latency and ~1.2% errors for 9 minutes while primary node was flapping. We served reduced capacity during failover.

marisa: closing pager for now, keeping incident open for vendor follow-up and postmortem. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident 2635000000 acknowledged closed by marisa at 23:18 UTC.

marisa: filing postmortem draft and assigning action items to infra and hw teams.

ellie-cs: will follow up with customer with summary and compensation offer if needed. :+1:
